idiom.source: qb/llm/qb.llm.md: addRefActor<T>() (same-core child, onInit run synchronously) + kill(); the fib and fork-join-create adapters
idiom.note: a granted node creates its children with addRefActor and push<>es each a TryGenerate; a node reports its subtree with one push<Report> and kills itself; the root's child i lives on VirtualCore i % cores, created there by a per-core planter

caveats: qb's VirtualCores are pinned one per CPU from the harness's set -- the mechanism qb is built on. CAF and SObjectizer are given the same treatment through their own APIs (caf::thread_hook, so_5 work-thread factory), so the CPU budget is identical and no framework is measured with its placement mechanism switched off
wait=1 maps to setLatency(0) (busy-spin, 100% CPU per core); wait=0 maps to a park cap on a condition variable that is signalled on every enqueue
qb is compiled with QB_WITH_LOGGING enabled. Logging work emitted inside the workload window is included; the runtime log level is not inferred from the build configuration

qb has no cross-core spawn: a node lives on its parent's VirtualCore, so with cores=2 the root's children i with i % 2 == 0 and their subtrees run on core 0, the others on core 1, and nothing balances the two -- at the defaults 31 145 nodes against 28 845; the pools place every node dynamically -- see benchmarks/savina/uct.md

the root's children on another core are created by a planter actor of that core on one Plant event per core (created before the window, not counted in the messages): qb's way to create an actor on another VirtualCore

every node is alive until the tree's report wave; the cap of 60 000 nodes is the common comparison cell for every framework: qb 3.2.1's actor id was a 16-bit slot per VirtualCore (65 534 live actors), which held the default and not Savina's 200 000; since 3.3.0 the id is 64-bit with a 24-bit ordinary slot per VirtualCore (16 711 679), and the canonical 200 000 verifies as a separate document (--param nodes=200000) -- see benchmarks/savina/uct.md
